title: Closed vocabularies
description: Closed vocabularies of the data pipeline (docs/DATA-PIPELINE.md). Each entry of $defs is a JSON Schema (enum, or anyOf of an enum and patterns) referenced as vocab.json#/$defs/<name>; x-terms carries one record per term (x-* keys are ignored by JSON Schema validators). First filled 22 Oct 2026 from /work/.wt-px/raw-data.csv (42,298 rows), data/catalog/unit_aliases.json and model/lqm.py.

fact_type.description: Fact types (DATA-PIPELINE §2). x-terms: description and the measure slots a fact of this type may fill.

score.description: A score the source gives for one entry (a cell, a printed number, a chart point).

run-score.description: The score of one run of a measure whose value is a mean of runs (DATA-PIPELINE §5.2 step 4, mean-of-runs): `term` = its metric, `scale` as a score; a fact carries `run` (the run's id), a table cell's run is its row key.

metric-definition.description: What a metric measures, as the source defines it (formula, scale, bounds).

headline-metric.description: The source's designated headline metric (or the metric it ranks by).

cost.description: A money amount the source gives for one run or entry (spend or estimate).

currency.description: The currency of a cost; `term` = a currency of this vocabulary.

unit.description: What one cost or usage figure covers (per task, per suite...); `term` = a unit of this vocabulary (usage and spend share it).

cost-basis.description: How the cost was obtained, in the source's words; `term` = a cost basis of this vocabulary.

cost-method.description: How the cost was computed, in the source's words; `term` = a cost method of this vocabulary.

price-table.description: The prices the source applied (per class, with their date when stated).

price-tier.description: The price tier the cost was computed or billed at (`term`: a price kind other than standard, e.g. flex, batch): re-priced to standard by the tier's proven uniform factor (prices.json).

tokens-in.description: Input tokens (uncached input when the source separates cache).

tokens-total.description: Total tokens with no class split (input plus output in one figure): usable only through a uniform factor, or for ratios within one model (DATA-PIPELINE §2).

reasoning-included-in-out.description: Whether the output tokens include the reasoning tokens: `term` true or false (vocab boolean), read as such.

cached-share.description: Share of input served from cache, as the source states it.

requests.description: Number of requests or calls of the run.

tokens-in-per-request.description: Input tokens of each request of the run, or the largest of them (per-call size): with `requests`, it decides whether a long-context price tier applies (DATA-PIPELINE §5.3 step 1).

model-name.description: A model's display name as the source writes it.

model-api-id.description: A model's API id / slug as the source writes it.

route.description: Through what the model was called (maker API, reseller, host, router, self-hosting); `term` = a routes.json id when the route is registered.

mode.description: A request parameter or product mode that selects another key (Pro, Deep Think...).

effort-label.description: A label the source gives to a configuration ("high", "lowest effort setting", "標準").

effort-setting.description: A setting line read in code or config (the source's own call, a harness or router config), with where it was read.

thinking-on.description: Thinking enabled with no level (a `-thinking` id, AA "(Reasoning)", enable_thinking: true).

no-effort-sent.description: The source states that no effort / thinking parameter was sent.

config-history.description: A config file's history over an interval (commits showing the same setting).

thinking-budget.description: A thinking token budget (exact count as written).

tools-regime.description: Which tools the model had (with tools, without tools, code execution...).

run-date.description: The day (or datetime) the run took place; a per-run timestamp counts as one.

run-date-convention.description: The source documents that its row or run ids encode the run date (e.g. manual-YYYYMMDD-…): `pattern` = a regex with a named group `date` (YYYYMMDD). Cited in run_date, it gives the measure's row key or run-id a stated run date. Only a documented convention (written, with its quote) counts.

run-id.description: The source's id of a run.

version.description: Benchmark, protocol or board version (the campaign).

early-access.description: The run used a pre-release / early-access model.

harness.description: The agent, CLI or evaluation framework that ran the model.

judge.description: The judge (model or panel) that graded this entry, per row when it varies.

aggregation.description: Which runs a mean covers (number of runs, epochs, which were excluded).

failure.description: Anomaly: the run did not complete or hit an infrastructure error.

cap.description: Anomaly: a declared cap (tokens, turns, dollars), scored.

restated-from.description: The number is copied from another publication (named).

same-runs-as.description: The source states these are the same runs as another document's.

evaluated-by.description: Who ran the evaluation, when it is not the publisher.

component-of.description: This setup is a component of a composite (with its weight).

items.description: Optional, never read by the tree: number of items.

attempts.description: Optional, never read by the tree: attempts per item.

note.description: Optional, never read by the tree: anything else worth keeping.

legacy-row.description: Migration (DATA-PIPELINE §8.1): one row of today's raw-data.csv, verbatim (the CSV record as its value, form legacy). A legacy measure carries it as it is: the build gives it today's status and applies none of the tree's steps.

effort-order.description: A chart point's rank among its series' points in increasing cost (or tokens) order, 'k/n', where the source states the points are the model's effort levels (a caption, title, legend or the text: 'reasoning-effort scaling'); computed by rule chart-effort-order from that statement (the maintainer, 26 Oct).

closed_term_fact_types.description: Fact types whose `term` is required and checked against a vocabulary (fact type → vocabulary). A thinking-budget's term is its token count (digits); a score's term is its metric.

measure_slot.description: Slots of a measure's `facts` (DATA-PIPELINE §3, plus the slots the tree reads that §3's example omits). x-terms: allowed fact types (null = any) and whether the slot takes a list.

value.description: The measured value (a score, or for a cost-only measure a cost).

runs.description: Per-run values of a measure whose value is a mean of runs (mean-of-runs: recomputed without the failed runs).

model.description: Facts naming the model (names, API ids, mode).

usage.description: Token / request usage of the run.

spend.description: The run's cost with its currency, unit, basis, method and price table.

route.description: Route chain facts: the only slot the route chain reads (a harness fact goes here only when the harness is a step of the chain, e.g. Inspect's provider prefix).

harness.description: Harness facts as a setup field (not read by the route chain).

setup.description: Facts proving the setup fields (harness, tools regime, metric, headline).

other.description: Facts kept for the verifier, never read by the tree.

legacy.description: The legacy row this measure carries (migration only; no other slot is read).

level.description: Certainty level of a source fact as the agent writes it (DATA-PIPELINE §1-2). `computed`: a derived value with its rule and inputs, recomputed by the build.

written.description: The source states it: printed number, data-file value, code/config line, API id, label.

read.description: Measured off a chart's geometry (pixels); needs a chart-pixel precision.

computed.description: A value derived from cited inputs by a stated rule (`rule`, `inputs`): the build recomputes it and refuses it when it differs (e.g. input − cache read).

source-estimate.description: A value the source did not measure on this run (imputed, projected, filled, "estimated").

not-established:absent.description: The source does not state it.

not-established:contradictory.description: The source, or two facts, state two things.

field_level.description: Level of a measure field computed by the build (status report; never written by agents).

computed.description: Produced by the build with a rules.json rule from accepted inputs.

fact_form.description: Where in the saved copy the fact sits; decides whether a quote is required (x-terms.quote).

prose.description: Running text of a page or paper.

table-cell.description: A cell of a table printed in a page (HTML/Markdown/PDF table).

label.description: A label (legend, column header, model display string, board label).

code.description: A code or config line (source's call, harness or router config).

image-text.description: A number or label printed on an image (written).

data-file.description: A value of a saved data file (CSV/JSON/YAML), proven by sha256 + locator.

chart.description: A point read off a chart's geometry (level read; vector paths are written).

legacy.description: A row of today's raw-data.csv (the legacy proof: its ref and confound text), accepted as it is until its source is converted.

precision_model.description: Precision model of a value (an attribute, never a level).

printed.description: Rounding of a printed number: one unit of its last digit (step).

chart-pixel.description: Reading sd of a chart point (sd in the value's unit or px with the chart's calibration).

exact.description: Exact (vector path, integer count, data file at full precision).

unit.description: Cost / usage units: every distinct non-empty `unit` of /work/.wt-px/raw-data.csv (22 Oct 2026), x-rows = its row count. x-aliases = data/catalog/unit_aliases.json (publisher → {label: unit}). Usage and spend share this list.
enum: USD whole-run cost estimate (cost_usd_estimate, not per case)

metric.description: Score metrics: every distinct non-empty `score_metric` of /work/.wt-px/raw-data.csv (22 Oct 2026), x-rows = its row count. A setup's `metric` and `headline.metric`, a score fact's or score column's `term`, are terms of this list: DATA-PIPELINE §5.2 step 5 compares them as terms. lqm.bound/kind read the spelling (a '%' means a 0-100 scale). `none` (added 23 Oct 2026): a cost-only setup, whose rows carry no score (its metric and headline are `none`; no score fact can be on it).
enum: author average 1-10 (5 criteria incl. cost points)
core pair accuracy pct macro 13 families

score_scale.description: How a score is written in the source (required on score facts and score columns). The rule scale-conversion converts fraction ↔ percent exactly (and percent-from-counts a count) to the setup metric's scale; never inferred from the size of the value.

raw.description: the metric's own units (Elo, counts, points, an index)

counts.description: 'k of N', 'k/N', 'k out of N': percent-from-counts gives 100·k/N (exact) on a percent metric, k/N on a fraction metric

currency.description: Currencies seen in the data's units and flags (USD, CNY incl. yuan/RMB, JPY). A cents unit stays USD; the unit carries the scale.

cost_basis.description: Cost bases (DATA-PIPELINE §5.3.2). x-terms.legacy_flags: regex over today's confound text used to map legacy rows (migration; flag-map.json will own it). list-estimate is reached through the methods mapped to it.

billed.description: What the provider invoiced for this run.

list-estimate.description: The run's own tokens at a stated list price, or a CLI's total_cost_usd (written, DATA-PIPELINE §1).

router-billed.description: What a router (OpenRouter...) charged for this run.

subscription.description: Covered by a plan / subscription: no per-run price (out:cost-basis).

cost_method.description: Cost methods (DATA-PIPELINE §5.3.2), derived from today's confound flags. x-terms: basis it implies and legacy_flags (regex, first match in this order wins; order = x-order). Coverage: `validate.py --legacy-coverage raw-data.csv`.

publisher-table.description: The publisher applied its own price table to the run's tokens (AA cost per task, a board's prices).

library-table.description: A library's price table applied to the run's tokens (litellm, runcost, tokencost: litellm-style price tables, DATA-PIPELINE §5.3.2).

cli-total.description: A CLI's or harness's own total (Claude Code total_cost_usd, Codex...).

router-invoice.description: A router's invoice / usage cost for the run.

tokens×list.description: The source multiplied the run's tokens by the maker's list price.

unstated.description: The source does not say how the cost was obtained.

x-not-methods.simulated-cost: classified per source at migration (DATA-PIPELINE §5.3.2): computed from this run's tokens → tokens×list, otherwise the level source-estimate (flag-map.json)
x-not-methods.reprice-YYYY-MM-DD / cache-cut / prev-co: our own repricing (computed, prev), not the source's method
x-not-methods.price-date / cache-price-date: a price-date fact, not a method
x-not-methods.digitised-cost / digitized-*: the fact's form and level (chart, read), not a method
x-not-methods.cost / cost-note / cost-source / cost-pe: free text: needs the source re-read

anomaly.description: Anomaly types (fact types failure / partial / cap) and their effect (DATA-PIPELINE §5.2.4).

failure.effect: out:failed-run; a mean including it is recomputed by mean-of-runs when per-run values are written

partial.effect: out:partial unless the source scores missing items as wrong

route_class.description: Route classes (DATA-PIPELINE §4 routes.json). The chain is applied harness → router / reseller / host → maker.

reseller.description: The maker's model resold (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure).

host.description: Open weights served by a third party (Fireworks, Together, DeepInfra, Groq).

harness.description: Harness / CLI (Inspect, Pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI, IronBee...).

self-hosted.description: vLLM, SGLang... The maker's defaults and conversions do not apply.

configuration.description: Configuration ids a model can offer (models.json configurations; DATA-PIPELINE §4). think-<n>: thinking on with a budget of n tokens (exact count as written; the build merges budgets within 5 %). In the fit: every id but think-<n> (out:budget-config). In models.json a model whose thinking takes any budget lists the family `think-<budget>` with budget_min / budget_max. between-tools (23 Oct 2026): Sonnet 5.5's thinking: {type: between_tools}; in the fit like every configuration of a model's list (coordinator, 26 Oct 2026). x-terms.in_fit false would keep a term recorded but out of the fit (none does today).

think.kind: thinking on, no level (on-off models without levels)

between-tools.kind: thinking: {type: between_tools} (Anthropic, Claude Sonnet 5.5): up-front thinking off, thinking between tool calls; accepted with effort low, medium or high only
between-tools.note: added 23 Oct 2026 (merge of the registry parts): documented by Anthropic as a thinking setting; it combines with an effort level (low, medium or high). Kept out of the fit at first (in_fit false); in the fit since 26 Oct 2026 (coordinator: a configuration of Sonnet 5.5's list, fitted like every configuration of a model's list). `regex`: how a setting line names it (thinking: {type: "between_tools"}).

solo.kind: only for a model whose list is [solo]

configuration_not_established.description: Configuration values the build can compute that are not established (all → out:effort-not-established). Today's data spells some of them (req-*, app-*, scalar).

nothink_spelling.description: Spellings of thinking off seen in today's data (confound text of the nothink / req-nothink rows of raw-data.csv). x-terms.kind: setting (an effort-setting or thinking-off fact read in code), label (a thinking-off label fact), name (a name that selects nothink in models.json names). x-terms.rows: rows whose confound or ref matches (case-insensitive).

none (label).note: a reasoning-effort legend or column whose value is 'none' (OpenAI charts: reasoning effort none = no reasoning; coordinator 26 Oct)

no reasoning.note: a row label 'GPT 5.4 (no reasoning)' (arxiv-2604.18934; coordinator 28 Oct)

Reasoning:disabled.note: a row label 'Claude Sonnet-4.5 (Reasoning:disabled)' (arxiv-2601.13206; coordinator 28 Oct)

think_spelling.description: Spellings of thinking on with no level seen in today's solo / req-enabled / req-thinking / think-unstated rows (re-read at migration into think).

Thinking / Reasoning (bare label).note: a column or legend labelled only 'Thinking' or 'Reasoning' (Gemini model cards): thinking on, no level (coordinator, 27 Oct)

reason_code.description: Status reason codes named in DATA-PIPELINE §5-6 (status report). Decisions add in:decision:<id> / out:decision:<id>. A legacy measure (migration) has legacy:in or legacy:out:<why> (today's admission: legacy:out:comment, :no-group, :model-not-in-fit-list, :effort-not-in-efforts, :no-value), and lqm.load's outcome as legacy:out:<code>.

out:no-proof.description: a fact used lacks a locator (or a required quote)

out:model-not-established.description: model not accepted or not in models.json

out:effort-not-established.description: configuration not established, or not in the model's list

out:value-not-established.description: value not established (absent, assumed or ambiguous; contradictory has its own code)

out:failed-run.description: failure anomaly, or a mean including a failed run not recomputable

out:not-headline.description: metric is not the setup's headline

out:uninformative.description: score at the floor or ceiling while the others are not (cost kept)

out:superseded.description: replaced within its campaign (kept as prev)

out:composite.description: composite row dropped by lqm.load's composites rule (a component measured)

out:single-couple.description: group with fewer than 2 accepted couples of fit models

out:cost-not-comparable.description: unrepriced cost whose price change is not uniform across classes

out:cost-single-couple.description: cost subset with fewer than 2 couples

out:saturated.description: group saturated at a bound (every couple at 0 % or 100 %), dropped by lqm.load

maker.description: Makers (models.json maker, publishers.json maker). Ids = lqm.MAKER_PUBLISHER's publisher spellings; x-terms.org = the spelling lqm.is_home matches in flags; x-terms.lqm_provider = lqm.provider(). `other` = any maker outside lqm's eight (lqm.provider gives it 'other'); it is never a publisher's maker (no home effect). Add a maker here before it gets its own scales in lqm.

lqm_flag.description: Confound flag spellings model/lqm.py (load, is_home) and model/validation/ratio_baseline.py read in the fit table; the build regenerates them from facts. <Org> = maker.x-terms.org.

EAP-run.from_facts: early-access fact, or run upper bound before released

restated-from:<Org>.reads: lqm.is_home: home when <Org> is the model's maker

restated-from:.reads: lqm.is_home: any other restatement is not home

as reported by <Org>.reads: lqm.is_home (substring, also in the harness column)
as reported by <Org>.from_facts: legacy spelling; the build writes vendor-reported:<Org>

<Org>-reported.from_facts: legacy spelling; the build writes vendor-reported:<Org>

prev.reads: none today (DATA-PIPELINE §6: written for replaced values)

fit_column.description: Columns of the fit tables (today's raw-data.csv header) and what reads them.

rule_id.description: Rule ids of rules.json (DATA-PIPELINE §4): deduction rules then standing rules. Standing rules added 23 Oct 2026 for the decisions of DATA-PIPELINE §4 (prices) and §9: configurations-per-model, cost-method-unstated-single, base-price-retired-last-list, base-price-charged-never-applied.

closed-harness-label.description: a closed harness's label is the level sent, flagged (the maintainer, 26 Oct 2026)

route-presumed-maker-api.description: no route named: the maker's API is presumed, flagged (the maintainer, 26 Oct 2026)

chart-effort-order.description: the k-th of n points of an effort chart is the model's k-th level when it has n levels (the maintainer, 26 Oct)

thinking-on-default-level.description: thinking on, no level, on a model with levels and no think: the maker's documented effort default (the maintainer's judgement, 26 Oct)

run-before-shutdown.description: a closed model's run with no stated end lies before its maker API ids stopped serving it (26 Oct)

complement-of-percent.description: 100 − a stated percentage (an error or refusal rate printed, its complement held), exact (26 Oct)

legacy_effort.description: Effort values of today's raw-data.csv outside configuration ∪ configuration_not_established, and where they go at migration (flag-map.json effort_values).

none.to: re-read: nothink spelling or not established

fast-mode.to: a setup attribute (fast mode), configuration re-read

nt-<level>.to: a tools regime (no tools) = setup; the configuration is <level>

wayback.description: a Wayback Machine capture (url with its timestamp)

commit.description: a repository commit (commit id, its date)

fetch.description: our own saved fetch (file + sha256, its time)

interval_from_basis.description: Why an interval starts where it does (DATA-PIPELINE §4).

release.description: configuration served as itself from the release

earliest-capture.description: no stated date: earliest capture showing it

interval_to_basis.description: Why an interval ends where it does.

stated.description: the change the document states (redirect, shutdown...)

last-capture.description: last capture still showing it (the next one does not)

level_mapping_rule.description: How a route maps a requested level (routes.json).

budget.description: model without an effort parameter: level → token budget (budget-converted)

mapping_result.description: What a route mapping can yield besides a configuration id.

cache-write-30m.description: OpenAI 30-minute cache write (GPT-6 pricing tables, 23 Oct 2026)

cache-write-12h.description: OpenAI 12-hour cache write (GPT-6 pricing tables, 23 Oct 2026)

price_kind.description: Kinds of price entries. Only `standard` is ever a base price; promotions and off-peak are recorded and flagged.

headline_basis.description: How a setup's headline metric was chosen (DATA-PIPELINE §4).

ranked-by.description: no designation: the metric the source ranks by

only-metric.description: the source reports a single metric for this benchmark (one score column per model, e.g. a sub-benchmark column of a board ranked by its total): that metric is the headline, evidence = the table (coordinator, 26 Oct)

boolean.description: A yes/no fact's term (reasoning-included-in-out): the build reads the term, never the level alone.
